card.name: Stop-the-drug warning phrases
card.fires_on: Small words inside warnings about stopping a drug or evaluating a patient right away, such as "of" in "at the first appearance of skin rash", "should" before "be evaluated", and "immediately" after "withdrawn". Also fires occasionally partway through a drug name or number.

modes.label: Discontinue at first sign
modes.description: Linking word in the standard instruction to stop the drug at the first appearance of rash.
modes.example: use of the drug should be discontinued at the first appearance<< of>> skin rash or any other

modes.label: Evaluate or withdraw promptly
modes.description: Words like should or immediately in instructions to evaluate the patient or withdraw the drug if signs appear.
modes.example: If such signs or symptoms are present, the patient<< should>> be evaluated immediately.

modes.label: Stray drug-name or number pieces
modes.description: Occasional hits inside a drug name or a dose number.
modes.example: Rare reports of cyan<<oc>>obalamin deficiency occurring with acid-sup

card.writes: Little clear effect; it weakly promotes words like satisfactory and acceptable and suppresses words like danger and necessary.
